features.verification: cd backend && python -m pytest tests/test_support_chat_ws.py -k broadcast
features.evidence: 16/16 tests in backend/tests/test_support_chat_ws.py pass (7 manager unit + 6 real-WS endpoint via TestClient + 3 broadcast via FakeWebSocket/async client). Non-vacuous: disabled both broadcast_message() calls in support.py, confirmed exactly the 3 broadcast tests failed, restored, reconfirmed green. Regression: 40/42 across test_support_chat_ws.py+test_support.py+test_admin.py; the 2 failures are the same pre-existing background-order-provisioning timing flake independently confirmed unrelated to this diff via git stash (fails identically with changes removed) on 3 separate occasions this session. 4 real bugs found and fixed while building this: (1) MissingGreenlet on message.attachments lazy-load inside broadcast_message - fixed with an explicit db.refresh(message, attribute_names=["attachments"]); (2) WS endpoints held a DB session open for a connections entire lifetime, leaking idle-in-transaction sessions - fixed by scoping the session to just the connect-time auth check; (3) main.py lifespan fired real background scheduler jobs (order recovery, catalog sync) on every TestClient startup with no test-environment guard, eventually deadlocking schema resets - fixed with an ENVIRONMENT!="test" guard; (4) TestClient.websocket_connect, when combined with a concurrent HTTP POST on the same portal thread, deadlocks non-deterministically on this Windows/anyio stack - worked around by proving FR-C105s broadcast wiring via FakeWebSocket + the normal async client fixture instead (real two-socket delivery over an actual connection is separately proven by FR-C103/C104s own TestClient tests, which never mix in a concurrent POST). **5th real bug found during live production verification, 2026-11-18, AFTER this was first marked passing - documented here rather than opening a new FR since it's a defect in this FR's own delivery, not new scope:** every real broadcast on beta silently failed with zero exceptions anywhere visible - WS connect/accept/reject all worked through the real Dokploy/Traefik proxy (confirmed via two live external test scripts and a third run from inside the backend container's own loopback, ruling out the proxy/network entirely), but no message ever reached a connected client. Root cause, found only after adding structured logging to ws_manager.py (commit e6d0123) and reading beta's own logs: serialize_message() passed message.created_at - a raw datetime - straight into websocket.send_json(), which uses plain json.dumps with no datetime encoder (unlike the REST response path, which goes through FastAPI's own encoder and never hit this); ConnectionManager's best-effort except-and-drop swallowed the TypeError on every single broadcast. Fixed (commit 7349a62) by serializing created_at to isoformat() before it reaches send_json, matching the pattern already used for last_message_at in the same function. Also fixed the test gap this exposed: FakeWebSocket.send_json previously just appended the raw dict without ever actually calling json.dumps, so the existing 16/16 passing suite could not have caught this class of bug - it now round-trips every payload through json.dumps/loads like Starlette's real send_json does; reran the full suite after the fix (29/30 locally against a disposable Postgres via Docker, same 1 pre-existing unrelated order-settling flake, 0 new failures) and separately proved true end-to-end delivery live against the real public beta.triptel.co domain (register -> create ticket -> open a real wss:// socket -> POST a reply -> receive it over the socket, verified via a throwaway script, succeeded).

features.behavior: Share an order/package from the chat UI
features.evidence: `npm run build` compiles clean. SharePicker.tsx reuses existing fetches (api.getMyESIMs; api.getCountries/getCountryProducts, the same two calls /explore already makes) rather than a new search endpoint; selecting an item posts through the exact same POST /support/tickets/{id}/messages a text reply uses. GET /orders/my-esims gained order_id (orders.py) - purely additive, confirmed non-regressive by stashing just that file and rerunning a failing esim-status test: it failed identically either way, confirming the failure is the same pre-existing background-order-provisioning timing issue (this disposable test environment's checkout provisioning now appears to fail to settle within 10s on most runs, not just occasionally - worth a dedicated look sometime, but unrelated to this diff and already documented multiple times this session). Same no-browser-automation-tool caveat as FR-C203/FR-C204 for the picker's interactive behavior. **Real bug found live on beta after shipping, fixed same day (2026-11-18):** the share picker always sends body="" when sharing with no extra text - Starlette's multipart parser treats an empty string for a required Form(...) field as the field being absent entirely, 422'ing before post_message's own validation ever ran. Fixed by giving body a Form("") default on both ticket-creating and reply endpoints. New test test_sharing_a_package_with_no_extra_text_still_works, confirmed non-vacuous (fails identically with Form(...) restored), confirmed fixed live on beta with a fresh throwaway account.

`npm run build` compiles clean. useSupportSocket reconnects on an unexpected close with exponential backoff (1s/2s/4s/8s/16s/30s cap), skipping retries entirely on the server's own 4401/4403 rejection codes (nothing a retry could fix). onReconnect fires only on an actual drop-then-reconnect and LiveTicketThread wires it to re-fetch the ticket, catching anything missed while disconnected - plus a visible 'Live updates paused' notice with a manual Refresh button while connected is false, never a hard error. This completes all 6 frontend widget FRs (FR-C201-C206). Same no-browser-automation-tool caveat as the other panel FRs for watching an actual drop/reconnect cycle happen live - the reasoning is otherwise directly inspectable from the code.
